source_name: Association of Serbian Banks (UBS-ASB) conference presentations — vendor decks naming bank deployments
why_relevant: Regional banking-association conference proceedings host vendor slide decks (e.g. Halcom ONE cloud-certificate integration into bank digital channels) that disclose architecture and often named deployments. Serbian/regional events regularly cover Montenegrin deployments because vendors serve both markets.

source_name: Privredna komora Crne Gore (Chamber of Economy) — saopštenja / contract-signing announcements
why_relevant: Chamber announcements name winning vendor consortia for national digitalisation projects (e.g. eKomora awarded to a consortium of Crnogorski Telekom, Montex elektronika, Axians Crna Gora, Čikom and WinSoft). This maps the ME supplier bench that also sells into banks, and is one of the few places where a Montenegrin contract award is stated publicly.

source_name: OTP Group Investor Relations - Reports (quarterly reports, investor presentations, CKB Group Montenegro segment)
why_relevant: OTP Bank Nyrt. is the parent of CKB (Crnogorska komercijalna banka), the largest bank in Montenegro. OTP's quarterly Stock Exchange Reports and investor presentations break out 'CKB Group (Montenegro)' as a named foreign subsidiary segment with after-tax profit, net interest margin, loan/deposit volumes and FX-adjusted growth - far richer and faster than anything CKB publishes locally.

source_name: OTP Group quarterly conference call presentation deck (Montenegro subsidiary slides)
why_relevant: The conference-call deck is the single densest recurring artefact containing Montenegro-level KPIs (profit contribution, NIM, cost/income, risk cost, digital/card metrics commentary) at group-audit quality and within ~6 weeks of quarter end.

source_name: NLB Group Investor Relations (NLB d.d., parent of NLB Banka AD Podgorica)
why_relevant: NLB d.d. is a Ljubljana Stock Exchange / LSE GDR listed issuer and 99.87% owner of NLB Banka AD Podgorica (3rd largest bank in Montenegro after the Komercijalna banka Podgorica merger). Group annual reports and quarterly presentations disclose Montenegro as a reportable geographic segment: profit before tax, loans, deposits, market share, employees, branch counts.

source_name: NLB financial reports PDF repository (nlb.si investor-relations/financial-reports, year-foldered)
why_relevant: Predictable year-foldered PDF store holding NLB Group annual reports and every quarterly results presentation; the mechanical backbone for a longitudinal Montenegro segment time series.

source_name: Erste Group Bank AG - Financial Reports (annual/interim reports, CBCR disclosure)
why_relevant: Erste Group owns Erste Bank AD Podgorica (4th largest bank in Montenegro, ~13.8% market share). Erste's annual report and the CRD-mandated country-by-country reporting annex list Montenegro explicitly (turnover, pre-tax profit, tax, employees), and Montenegro appears in the 'Other' / Savings Banks & other subsidiaries segment discussion.

source_name: Erste Group Montenegro country/International Desk page
why_relevant: Group-maintained descriptive page on the Montenegrin subsidiary (entry 2009 via Opportunity Bank, branch footprint, coverage). Useful for actor-map maintenance and detecting network/footprint changes between annual reports.

source_name: Addiko Bank AG - Financial Reports (Addiko Group, parent of Addiko Bank AD Podgorica)
why_relevant: Addiko Group (Vienna-listed) reports by country and by focus segment (Consumer/SME). Montenegro is one of its six markets, and quarterly earnings releases plus results presentations give Montenegro-level gross performing loans, NIM, NPL and digital-channel/consumer-lending commentary that is not published locally in comparable form.

source_name: Ziraat Bankasi Investor Relations / Integrated Annual Report (parent of Ziraat Bank Montenegro AD)
why_relevant: Ziraat Bank Montenegro AD is a 100% Ziraat subsidiary (licensed 2015, Podgorica HQ, branches in Podgorica, Bar, Budva). Ziraat's integrated annual report contains a recurring international-subsidiaries section giving Montenegro total assets, loans, deposits and capital - one of the few English-language time series on this small bank.

source_name: AIK Banka a.d. Beograd (AikGroup) corporate/investor disclosures - parent of Hipotekarna banka AD Podgorica
why_relevant: AikGroup states that Hipotekarna banka in Montenegro is a group member alongside Gorenjska banka (SI) and AikLeasing/MV Investment (RS). AIK is a Belgrade Stock Exchange issuer, so its consolidated annual report and group presentations should carry Montenegro-level contribution - the only group-level view on Hipotekarna, a top-4 Montenegrin bank strong in cards/acquiring.

source_name: Serbian Securities Commission (Komisija za hartije od vrednosti) issuer filings register - AIK Banka
why_relevant: Statutory filing register for Serbian issuers; the authoritative route to AIK Banka consolidated annual/semi-annual reports containing the Montenegro (Hipotekarna) contribution when the bank's own IR page is thin.

source_name: Asseco South Eastern Europe Group annual/consolidated management reports (Payten - Montenegro payments segment)
why_relevant: Sector=both: ASEE (Warsaw-listed) is the parent of Payten Montenegro, the dominant regional card-processing/ATM-POS services provider serving Montenegrin banks. Its Payment Solutions segment reporting names Montenegro growth explicitly - a rare group-level, audited window on Montenegrin payments volumes and vendor share.

source_name: Asseco Poland Group consolidated management report (ASEE/Payten roll-up)
why_relevant: Ultimate parent's consolidated report repeats and sometimes expands the SEE payments narrative; useful cross-check and occasionally discloses Payten entity restructurings (e.g. transfer of Payten Montenegro to a holding company).

source_name: CKB (Crnogorska komercijalna banka) financial statements & OTP Group section
why_relevant: The Montenegrin subsidiary's own site hosts consolidated local annual reports (konsolidovani godisnji izvjestaj) and the group-affiliation page; the reconciliation point between OTP group segment figures and local statutory accounts.

source_name: Lovcen banka AD Podgorica - Izvjestaji o poslovanju
why_relevant: Annual business reports, financial statements and auditor reports back to ~2017 for a mid-size Montenegrin bank whose ownership chain (regional investor group) needs to be tracked; ownership/shareholder notes here are the entry point to any parent-group reporting.

source_name: Central Bank of Montenegro (CBCG) - bank-by-bank balance sheets, P&L and financial statements
why_relevant: Per-bank regulatory statements (NLB, Erste, Addiko, Hipotekarna, Lovcen, CKB, Ziraat...) give the independent local baseline against which foreign parents' segment figures can be reconciled, and the canonical roster of which Montenegrin banks have foreign parents at all.

source_name: Quartr - OTP Bank / listed parent-group earnings events, decks and call audio
why_relevant: Aggregates earnings-call audio, transcripts and slide decks per event for listed parents (OTP, and analogous pages for NLB/Erste/Addiko). Analyst Q&A is where Montenegro-specific colour (margins in euroised markets, subsidiary M&A) surfaces outside the formal reports.

source_name: Seeking Alpha / stockanalysis.com / Investing.com earnings-call transcripts for CEE parent groups
why_relevant: Transcript mirrors capture management's verbatim commentary naming Montenegro (e.g. euro/quasi-euro country margin headwinds covering Bulgaria, Slovenia, Croatia and Montenegro) - qualitative signal absent from the PDFs.

source_name: SeeNews - Montenegro company/banking news wire (group results reported for local subsidiaries)
why_relevant: Fast English-language reporting of subsidiary league tables and group-result read-throughs (e.g. CKB remaining Montenegro's top bank by profit and assets), useful as a trigger to fetch the underlying group filing.

source_name: FinancialReports.eu - filings index for NLB Banka AD / Asseco SEE and other parents
why_relevant: Indexes issuer filings across EU venues; a convenient discovery layer for locating group annual/interim reports and their attachments when issuer sites reorganise URLs.

source_name: EMIS company profile - Erste Bank AD Podgorica (and peer Montenegrin subsidiaries)
why_relevant: Commercial database with standardised financials and executive data for Montenegrin bank subsidiaries; useful for entity identifiers and cross-checks, but subscription-gated.

source_name: UBCG member banks directory (11 licensed banks)
why_relevant: Enumerates the full population of licensed Montenegrin banks that are association members - Addiko, Adriatic, CKB (OTP), Erste, Hipotekarna, NLB, Lovćen, Prva banka, Universal Capital, Zapad, Ziraat. Each entry snowballs into a bank IR/disclosure source for workstream A1.

source_name: UBCG 'Bankar' magazine / association publications
why_relevant: The association's periodical (Bankar, issue numbering in the 70s as of 2026) carries sector commentary, executive interviews and aggregate banking-sector figures - a recurring, citable serial for tracking industry narrative on payments, digitalisation and fees.

source_name: UBCG legislation tracker
why_relevant: Association-curated list of banking/payment laws and bylaws relevant to members - a shortcut to which regulatory changes the industry considers material, useful for anticipating payment-fee and AML rule changes.

source_name: Privredna komora Crne Gore (Chamber of Economy of Montenegro) - Odbori udruženja index
why_relevant: Index of the Chamber's 13 sector association boards. It is the entry point to the banking/finance/insurance board and the ICT board, each of which lists named company representatives - a cross-sector actor map covering banks, insurers and IT vendors in one place.

source_name: PKCG Odbor udruženja bankarstva, drugih finansijskih organizacija i osiguranja
why_relevant: Names ~23 member representatives spanning banks (Addiko, Adriatic, CKB, Erste, Hipotekarna, NLB, Prva, Universal Capital, Zapad, Ziraat), insurers (Lovćen, Grawe, UNIQA), the central bank and development institutions, plus board officers (president Miloš Miketić - Lovćen banka; secretary Almer Bećiragić). Broader than UBCG because it includes insurance and non-bank finance.

source_name: PKCG Odbor udruženja informacionih i komunikacionih tehnologija (ICT board)
why_relevant: Chamber ICT board roster identifies the IT/payment-technology vendor population inside the formal chamber structure - relevant for the payments/fintech half of sector=both and for spotting POS/fiscalisation vendors.
